# Results -- Study 261 (Put-Call-Ratio) on real monthly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: read the
hardcoded CBOE total put/call ratio at month-end; if it is in its top quintile of
expanding history (extreme fear), hold the S&P 500 for the next month, else hold
cash. Pinned against always-invested buy-and-hold, a continuous predictive
regression, a random-timing null, and sub-periods. **Price-only ^GSPC** (index
excludes dividends -- so buy-and-hold's true edge is even larger than shown).
As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| CBOE total put/call (hardcoded, month-end) + ^GSPC monthly via yfinance | 2003-01-31 -> 2025-12-31 | 276 months (240 active post-burn-in) | `8edbde520f70` |

Put/call ratio: mean **0.913**, std **0.107**. Burn-in = 36 months (expanding
quantile threshold). One full month of execution lag: the ratio at month-end t
sets the position held *through* month t+1.

## Continuous predictive regression (the cleanest test)

Next-month ^GSPC return regressed on the expanding-window put/call **z-score**
(HAC / Newey-West standard errors). A contrarian edge would show a **positive**
slope (high fear -> high forward return).

| Slope (per 1-sigma) | HAC *t* | R^2 | n |
|--------------------|---------|-----|---|
| **-0.0007** | **-0.16** | 0.0002 | 240 |

The slope is essentially zero (wrong sign, *t* = -0.16). **The put/call ratio
carries no predictive content for the next month's index return.**

## Extreme-fear timing rule vs buy-and-hold

| Strategy | Mean return | HAC *t* | Ann. Sharpe | Hit | Max DD |
|----------|------------|---------|-------------|-----|--------|
| Extreme-fear timing (gross) | **+2.18%/yr** | +1.02 | **+0.20** | 0.163 | -37.1% |
| Extreme-fear timing (net, 5 bps/switch) | +2.02%/yr | +0.95 | -- | -- | -- |
| **Buy & hold S&P (price-only)** | **+9.63%/yr** | +2.81 | **+0.64** | -- | -52.6% |

The rule is in-market only **26%** of months (64 switches over the sample). By
sitting in cash three-quarters of the time it forfeits ~7.5%/yr of index drift
for a modestly smaller drawdown -- a poor trade, with a **lower** Sharpe than
simply owning the index. Costs are *not* the problem (net is barely below gross);
the signal is.

## Conditional next-month return -- the killer

| State | Mean next-month return | HAC *t* | n |
|-------|------------------------|---------|---|
| After **extreme fear** (top quintile) | **+0.69%/mo** | +1.02 | 63 |
| After **calm** | +0.84%/mo | +3.11 | 177 |
| Difference (fear - calm) | **-0.15%/mo** | Welch *t* = -0.18 (p = 0.86) | -- |

Extreme-fear months are followed by returns *slightly below* calm months -- the
**opposite** sign of the contrarian-bottom claim, and statistically
indistinguishable from zero.

## Random-timing null

Drawing the same number of in-market months at random gives a mean in-market
return of **+0.82%/mo**; the fear-timed selection is **beaten by a random pick
61.5%** of the time (permutation p = 0.615). The signal carries no timing skill
beyond chance.

## Sub-period stability

| Period | Timing /yr | HAC *t* | n | Buy & hold /yr |
|--------|-----------|---------|---|----------------|
| 2006--2012 | -2.0%/yr | -0.41 | 84 | +3.7%/yr |
| 2013--2019 | +3.5%/yr | +1.91 | 84 | +11.6%/yr |
| 2020--2025 | +5.5%/yr | +1.69 | 72 | +14.3%/yr |

In **every** sub-period the timing rule underperforms simply owning the index,
and it never clears the *t* = 2 inference bar.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds an edge when one is planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`, planting
`fwd_ret = base + beta*(pcr - mean) + noise`), the predictive regression recovers
the planted contrarian slope monotonically:

| Planted contrarian beta | Slope HAC *t* |
|------------------------|---------------|
| 0.00 (null) | -0.95 |
| +0.15 (planted) | **+6.98** |
| +0.30 (strong) | **+14.81** |

The engine reads ~zero on the null and strongly positive when fear is genuinely
informative -- so the flat real-tape result is not a machinery failure.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Predictive-regression slope HAC *t* = -0.16 (wrong sign);
  extreme-fear months return *less* than calm months (Welch *t* = -0.18); a
  random in-market selection beats the fear-timed one 61% of the time. The
  put/call ratio measures fear well but does not forecast the index. The
  short (~23yr) sample is dominated by a few non-independent crisis spikes.
  Verdict: **NONE**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The timing rule earns +2.2%/yr against the index's
  +9.6%/yr with a *lower* Sharpe (0.20 vs 0.64), because it is in cash ~74% of
  the time. Net of costs it is the same story (costs are negligible here -- the
  edge simply does not exist). There is nothing to trade. Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Survivorship / sample -- named on the Signal axis.** The ^GSPC index is
  survivorship-clean, but the put/call history is short and the "extreme"
  tail rests on a handful of clustered episodes; price-only returns understate
  buy-and-hold's true (dividend-inclusive) advantage.
